# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 60 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 60 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_060_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 6 — The Extra Work of the Son of God

**60:1** "Lord," I said, "why did the slave do more than he was commanded? Why did he dig and clear the vineyard, when he had only been told to fence it?" "Listen," he said. "The slave is the Son of God, and the work he did beyond the commandment is a type of what he chose to do beyond what was required."

**60:2** "For the Son of God was not content merely to give the commandments to the people, but he himself bore their sins. This therefore is the additional work that the Son of God performed: he bore the sins of the people and suffered on their behalf."

**60:3** "When therefore he took counsel with the first-created angels regarding what reward should be given the slave for the additional work he had done, this is the deliberation concerning the flesh of the Son of God. For this flesh served the Spirit well and purely, not being defiled in any way in its conduct upon the earth. Therefore the reward was given to it."

**60:4** "The Father therefore took counsel with the Son and with the holy angels so that this flesh, which had served the Spirit blamelessly, should have some resting place and not lose the reward of its service. For every flesh that is found pure and unspotted, in which the Holy Spirit has dwelt, shall receive a reward."

**60:5** "You now have the interpretation of this parable." "I have it, lord," I said. "Lord," I continued, "hear me for one more moment." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "the flesh is fragile and perishable." "So it is," he said. "But this perishable nature cannot put on incorruption unless first the Holy Spirit is joined to it; for a person cannot put on incorruption unless clothed with it. Therefore when you have put on the Holy Spirit, put on the flesh also, and the flesh will be made subservient to the Spirit."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the pneumatological-christological argument closing Similitude 5.*
